question: how did it end? and what was the outcome from it?

answers: The Korean War ended when an armistice, which is the agreement created the Korean Demilitarized Zone to separate North and South Korea and allowed the return of prisoners, was signed. However, technically, the two Koreas are still at war, engaged in a frozen conflict. The war is considered to have ended at this point, even though there was no peace treaty. North Korea, nevertheless, claims that it won the Korean War.

history.content: does korean war have a different name?

Yes. In South Korea , the war is usually referred to as "625" or the "625 Upheaval''(yook - i-o dongnan ). On the other hand , the war is officially referred to as the Fatherland Liberation War '' ( Choguk haebang chǒnjaeng ) or alternatively the Chosǒn ( Korean ) War in North Korea. Additionally, the Korean War is 한국 전쟁 in South Korean Hangul, and it is 韓國 戰爭 in Hanja in South Korea. It is 조국 해방 전쟁 in North Korean Chosŏn'gŭl and 祖國 解放 戰爭 in Hanja in North Korea. In the U.S., it was initially described as a "police action" and has been referred to as "The Forgotten War" or "The Unknown War". In China, it is officially called the "War to Resist America and Aid Korea", but the terms "Chaoxian (Korean) War" in unofficial contexts and "Han (Korean) War" are also used in regions such as Hong Kong and Macau.
when did it start and end?
The Korean War started on 25 June 1950 and ended on 27 July 1953.
